purpose: Cetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching. It also helps with hives (raised, itchy skin welts). It works for both seasonal allergies (like hay fever) and year-round allergies (like pet dander or dust mites).
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it encounters something you are allergic to, and histamine is what causes all those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Cetirizine blocks the receptors in your body that histamine attaches to, so histamine cannot do its job of causing symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so histamine cannot get in — your symptoms stay away as a result.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, though this tends to be milder than older antihistamines. You may also notice a dry mouth, headache, stomach upset, or feeling tired. Some people feel a little dizzy as well.
warnings: Be careful driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, since it can cause drowsiness in some people. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cetirizine because it can increase drowsiness. Talk to your doctor before using it if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. It is generally safe, but always check with your pharmacist before giving it to young children or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 6 years and older, the usual dose is 5 mg to 10 mg once a day by mouth. Most people take it in the evening since it can cause drowsiness. Children between 2 and 5 years old are usually given 2.5 mg once a day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it around the same time each day for the best results.
